title: Monthly MRR report for the board deck
author: Priya Patel
summary: How I produce the MRR numbers for the monthly board deck: sanity-check payment health first, verify the revenue fact loaded, then pull the MRR rollup and hand the numbers to finance.

steps.title: Check payment pipeline health
steps.instruction: Open payment_health_daily and confirm yesterday's success_rate is above 0.97 for both providers. If it dipped, the revenue numbers may undercount — check with the on-call before reporting anything.
steps.why: A payment outage silently deflates MRR. Finance has been burned by this before — always rule it out first.
steps.tips: The saved query 'Payment success rate by provider' on this dataset is the fastest check.

steps.title: Verify fct_revenue loaded cleanly
steps.instruction: Open fct_revenue and check the dataset's last updated time and row-count trend. Use net_amount_usd for anything you report — gross_amount_usd includes refunded charges.
steps.why: fct_revenue is the canonical revenue source; every downstream number is wrong if this load was partial.
steps.tips: If latest is more than a day behind, ping Mike Rodriguez — the dbt mart job may have failed.

steps.title: Pull the MRR rollup
steps.instruction: Open mrr_monthly and run the saved query 'Monthly MRR trend by plan' for the last 12 months. Copy mrr_usd and net_new_mrr_usd into the board template.
steps.why: This table implements the official MRR definition (glossary term MRR) — never recompute it by hand from payments.
steps.sql:
SELECT month, plan, mrr_usd, net_new_mrr_usd
FROM analytics.marts.mrr_monthly
WHERE month >= DATEADD(month, -12, CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY month, plan;
steps.tips: Board deck wants plan-level rows plus a total — the total is the SUM over plans, not a separate table.

recorded.title: payment_health_daily
recorded.note: Always check this first after an incident-heavy month.

recorded.title: mrr_monthly
recorded.note: Saved query has the exact board cut.
